question: Why is separate discussion of ritual seats unnecessary in this sequence?
premises: In this sequence, the tree of difference is uprooted from its root.
When difference is uprooted, separate discussion of seats and related details is not fitting.
The supreme lord rests in the abode of his own power.
inference: Because the root of difference is removed and the supreme lord rests in his own power, no separate treatment of ritual seats is needed.
uncertainties: The technical nuance of 'āsanapakṣacarcā' may refer to specific ritual debates not fully recoverable from the verse alone.
plain_english: Here, since the tree of difference is uprooted from its very root, a separate discussion of seats and such matters is not fitting; for the supreme lord rests in the abode of his own power.
